clauses.reason: Executive Order 10843, signed 1959-10-09 (24 FR 8289), creates a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 ("create a Board of Inquiry"), gives it the powers and duties set forth in Title II of that Act, directs it to report to the President "on or before October 16,1959." and provides that after its report the board continues in existence until it is "terminated by the President". Later event: Executive Order 10848, signed 1959-10-14 (24 FR 8401, Federal Register of October 16, 1959), amends the second sentence in the penultimate paragraph of this order "to read as follows:" the Board shall report to the President in accordance with the provisions of section 206 of such Act on or before "October 19, 1959." Before the amendment the sentence ended "on or before October 16,1959."; after it the report date is October 19, 1959. The amendment moves a deadline by three days and leaves the creation of the board and its continued existence unchanged (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments); an amended report deadline is not an end. The only own-terms end is termination by the President. No held text records such a termination, and that absence is not proof that none occurred, so it is disclosed as an open earlier-end candidate; under the owner's report-deadline ruling an order of this kind that stayed on the books ends on its express revocation. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and" "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The cited source is the held Federal Register text of EO 12553; the dossier's located-provision records for the EO 12553 revocation of this order are American Presidency Project transcriptions, so they are not cited. The table on page 11 of the held text lists the number 10843 as entry 53 of 64 and 10848 as entry 54; on that page the text layer prints the numbers first and the subjects afterwards, and entry 53 of the subject list is "Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the steel industry", which agrees with the order's title. The alignment is by position, and a reviewer should confirm it against the page image. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective and take effect; the only hit is a word inside another order's subject line), so the signing date, 1986-02-25, is recorded; the filing date 1986-02-26 (the held text prints "Filed 2-26-86") and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 are the alternative readings, and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10843 (24 FR 8289, Federal Register of October 13, 1959), signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower and dated October 9, 1959; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: one whole-order clause covers the heading, the two recitals and the operative text: creation of a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947, with three named members, to inquire into the steel-industry dispute; the grant of the powers and duties set forth in Title II of that Act; the direction to report on or before October 16, 1959; and the provision that after its report the Board continues in existence until terminated by the President. Later event: EO 10848 (1959-10-14, 24 FR 8401) restates the report sentence with the date October 19, 1959. Ending: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 revokes the order and its amendment EO 10848 by number. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog notes (five machine hits) record the amendment by EO 10848 and the revocation by EO 12553.

(3) The OFR catalog notes and the number-citation scan of held texts show no instrument other than EO 10848 (an amendment) and EO 12553 (the revocation) acting on this order. savings.reason: EO 12553 has no saving, exception or pending-matters language attached to its revocation list (the held text was searched for except, notwithstanding, nothing in, saving and pending; the only hits are inside other orders' subject lines). The board's report and any later proceedings under the Labor-Management Relations Act rest on that statute and on the parties' acts, not on this order.
